baseline_models.focus_anchor: The reciprocal يَتَنَاهَوْنَ at word 3 governs عَن مُّنكَرٍ and is followed by the deed they enacted and the doing condemned.
baseline_models.mechanism: Reciprocal checking should interrupt an enacted wrong. Its absence removes the group's internal brake, allowing an occurrence of wrongdoing to become a recurring practice; the failed feedback is itself inside what the closing ذم condemns.

activation_trace.role: The literal image of rebuking and restraining supplies the missing reciprocal brake in the mechanism.
The morally ugly act that reason or law repels identifies what the absent brake should stop.
The two occurrences of enacted work connect the done wrong to the continuing practice produced by failed restraint.
Repeated temporal occurrence frames non-restraint and doing as an established pattern rather than one lapse.
The explicit word of blame evaluates the recurring practice, including the failure to check it.

changed_reading.before: They failed to tell one another not to commit a bad deed.
changed_reading.after: They maintained no mutual stopping practice, so enacted wrong met no internal resistance and became what the group characteristically kept doing.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The end or limit branch of ن ه ي in يَتَنَاهَوْنَ is enclosed by repeated كَانُوا and paired فَعَلُوهُ / يَفْعَلُونَ.
baseline_models.mechanism: Alongside reciprocal forbidding, the construction can activate failure to bring action to an endpoint. The first فعل names an accomplished wrong, while the second and repeated كون recast it as a state that keeps obtaining because no collective limit is reached.

activation_trace.role: The literal endpoint or extremity supplies a terminal boundary that the group's conduct never reaches.
Repeated production of an act turns the missing endpoint into continued enactment.
Occurrence through time stabilizes the no-end process as their habitual condition.
The blame formula marks this sustained lack of termination as reprehensible.

changed_reading.before: A prohibition was omitted on one occasion.
changed_reading.after: They did not bring one another's enacted wrong to a limit; an act that should have ended instead settled into their continuing way of acting.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: مُّنكَرٍ at word 5 carries both non-recognition and change into an unrecognized or disliked state, while يَتَنَاهَوْنَ names the absent mutual response.
baseline_models.mechanism: A group keeps wrong socially marked by recognizing, disavowing, and restraining it. When no member supplies that response, repeated enactment can erase the practical mark of strangeness: what should be rejected becomes familiar even while remaining blameworthy.

activation_trace.role: Opposition to recognition supplies the social marking problem attached to the focus noun.
Change into an unrecognized or disliked state supplies the normalization reversal caused by silence.
Mutual rebuke is the missing public act that would keep the wrong recognized as rejectable.
Continued enactment supplies the repetition through which an unchallenged wrong becomes familiar.

changed_reading.before: The wrong is fully evident, but nobody objects.
changed_reading.after: Their non-objection also disables the group's recognition practice: repeated wrong is no longer kept publicly marked as something alien and rejectable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The 5:62-63 parallel first presents accelerated harmful practice and then assigns a stopping function to learned custodians. Calling their failure صَنْع revises the focus from an evenly distributed lapse into a layered feedback failure: specialists who should cultivate and preserve limits can help manufacture the conditions in which everyone keeps acting.

activation_trace.role: The focus's reciprocal restraint remains the mechanism being redistributed across social roles.
The focus's enacted and recurring doing is what institutional non-restraint permits.
Speed as the opposite of delay makes the wrongdoing an accelerating practice in need of an active brake.
The defective illicit object gives the accelerated practice a concrete consumptive form.
Direct restraint in the parallel verse specifies the missing function that the focus distributes reciprocally.
Rabbinic knowledge supplies one institutional bearer of the neglected stopping function.
The learned keeper of a book supplies a second specialized bearer of corrective knowledge.
Making a thing turns neglected correction from empty inaction into participation in social production.

structural_cues: 5:62-63 repeat the لَبِئْسَ مَا كَانُوا frame, ending first in يَعْمَلُونَ and then in يَصْنَعُونَ.
5:63 names two specialist groups as the subject of the missing prohibition, whereas 5:79 broadens the failure to reciprocal group practice.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies speed, illicit consumption, named learned groups, direct prohibition, and making; I infer that neglected specialist correction helps produce the wider habit. The live alternative is that 5:63 and 5:79 condemn separate levels without a causal arrow between them.

changed_reading.before: Everyone equally failed to object to everyone else.
changed_reading.after: The reciprocal failure includes a broken institutional layer: those equipped to recognize and cultivate limits do not brake an accelerating practice, so their omission helps produce the group's recurring doing.

context_deltas.mechanism: Cessation in 5:73, desire-following and repeated straying in 5:77, then disobedience and limit-crossing in 5:78 turn the endpoint baseline into collective boundary governance. Mutual restraint should stop private inclination from becoming a followed group trajectory; without feedback, excess crosses its limit and persists.

activation_trace.role: The focus root's endpoint image anchors the model in a limit the group fails to reach.
Ending or reaching a terminal limit makes the same root explicitly operate as cessation of continuing speech.
Allegiant succession turns uncorrected inclination into a socially followed sequence.
The soul's inclination supplies the directional impulse that reciprocal limits should correct.
Three occurrences of departure from guidance trace drift propagating from a group to many and back to the group.
The middle, just position supplies the norm against which the group's drift is measurable.
An extended traversable path turns repeated drift into a sustained collective trajectory.
Departure from obedience names the refusal of the governing limit immediately before the focus.
Crossing the boundary and doing wrong supplies the terminal failure that mutual checking should prevent.

structural_cues: The branchless غ ل و occurrence at 5:77 word 5 explicitly places excess before desire-following and triple ض ل ل.
5:78 ends with ongoing يَعْتَدُونَ, and 5:79 immediately explains that persistence through absent reciprocal restraint.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies cessation, excess, desire-following, repeated drift, disobedience, and boundary-crossing; I infer a feedback system that should terminate collective drift. A narrower live alternative is simple verbal admonition with no claim about group trajectory.

changed_reading.before: They failed to tell one another to stop.
changed_reading.after: They failed to make excess end: no reciprocal boundary corrected desire-led drift, so transgression remained the group's ongoing way.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated blindness and deafness of 5:71 contrast with the ordered hearing, recognition, truthful identification, speech, and witness of 5:83. That contrast strengthens the non-recognition branch of مُّنكَر: mutual restraint is the final public stage of a social recognition circuit, and its absence can leave wrongdoing perceptually and verbally unmarked.

activation_trace.role: Non-recognition is the focus anchor recast as a failure of shared moral perception.
Reciprocal rebuke is the missing outward response that should follow recognition.
Repeated blindness of insight supplies closure at the perceptual entrance of the failed circuit.
Repeated loss of hearing and refusal to listen closes a second channel of corrective reception.
Hearing as understanding and response opens the contrasting receptive circuit.
Recognition by a trace or sign supplies explicit discrimination rather than moral unmarking.
Stable correspondence with reality gives recognition a determinate object against its opposite in مُّنكَر.
Knowledge made explicit supplies the public articulation that contrasts with silent non-restraint.

structural_cues: 5:71 repeats عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا on both sides of ثُمَّ تَابَ, marking relapse rather than a single sensory failure.
5:83 orders reception and response as hearing, visible affect, recognition, saying, and requested inclusion among witnesses.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a closed perception sequence and a later recognition-to-witness sequence; I infer that reciprocal restraint depends on converting perception into public corrective speech. The live alternative is that مُّنكَر is only a fixed moral category and the sensory contrast does not describe its social maintenance.

changed_reading.before: Wrongdoing is already recognized, and the only missing step is prohibition.
changed_reading.after: The prohibition fails as part of a larger recognition circuit: closed reception and absent public witness let enacted wrong lose its actionable social mark.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately after the focus, 5:80-81 replaces failed separation from wrong with proximity, support, and deliberate acquisition of allies. The social topology revises non-restraint from empty passivity into a possible mode of alignment: when members do not interrupt one another's wrong, nearness without a corrective gap can carry the practice forward and attach its consequence to the self.

activation_trace.role: The missing reciprocal restraint anchors the social relation that the following affiliation reframes.
The rejected ugly act remains the object from which corrective social distance should be created.
Love, support, and affiliation turn absence of correction into a positively maintained social bond.
Advancing forward makes alignment consequential rather than static.
The self in its own identity receives what the affiliative practice sends ahead.
Adhesion and lasting attachment extend social alignment into durable consequence.
Deliberate taking and acquisition makes affiliation an adopted relation, not mere coexistence.
Nearness without an intervening gap supplies the topology opposite to corrective separation.

structural_cues: 5:80 immediately repeats the لَبِئْسَ مَا frame after describing many who affiliate.
5:81 uses a counterfactual: belief would have prevented taking them as allies.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies affiliation, deliberate adoption, self-advancement, and lasting attachment immediately after the focus; I infer that non-restraint can enable or express alignment. The live alternative is that affiliation is an adjacent charge and not the mechanism of 5:79.

changed_reading.before: Their fault is passive silence toward another person's act.
changed_reading.after: Their silence can be socially affiliative: nearness and support leave no corrective gap, carry the practice forward, and bind its consequence to the participants themselves.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it combines the focus root's stream-end branch with later overflow and river branches to make a hydraulic social model. It remains anchored in يَتَنَاهَوْنَ through ن ه ي B004 and in the repeated focus فعل; downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for containment, never as the lexical translation of the ayah.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The ن ه ي inventory for يَتَنَاهَوْنَ includes water settling where a torrent ends, while the focus repeats enacted doing.

activation_trace.role: Water settling at the end of a stream supplies the unusual image of a terminal social basin.
Repeated production of action supplies what continues to enter the uncontained flow.
Easy abundant overflow triggers the flow side of the material analogy.
A vessel filled until it overflows supplies pressure and capacity within the flow model.
Continuous coursing supplies motion that requires a channel or endpoint.
A river cutting earth with flowing water supplies the channel against which the absent settling place is imagined.

changed_reading.before: No one verbally stopped a repeated wrong.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the group has no settling basin for action: wrongdoing keeps flowing because reciprocal restraint never gives it a terminal place to stop.

strongest_changes: The 5:62-63 near-parallel turns reciprocal non-restraint into a layered institutional production failure.
The 5:73-78 sequence strengthens an endpoint reading: desire-led drift becomes ongoing boundary-crossing because no collective feedback makes it end.
The immediate 5:80-81 affiliation sequence revises passive silence into possible proximity, support, and self-binding alignment.
The contrast between 5:71 and 5:83 expands prohibition into the public output of a recognition-to-witness circuit.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly restages the focus's roots and blame frame on both sides: act and manufacture before it, cessation and limit-crossing immediately before it, affiliation immediately after it, and receptive recognition farther after it. This made 5:79 read as a diagnosis of failed collective feedback rather than an isolated demand for admonition.
remaining_uncertainties: The balance between reciprocal forbidding and collective cessation in يَتَنَاهَوْنَ remains open.
The specialist responsibility in 5:63 may illuminate without causally producing the broader reciprocal failure in 5:79.
The affiliation in 5:80-81 may be a consequence adjacent to non-restraint rather than its social mechanism.
The hydraulic outlier is branch-licensed analogy only and should not control a plain rendering.
